survey: A beach ball lying on rippled sand, seen from slightly above and in front. Six gores (red, white, green, white, blue, white) meet at a purple cap set above and a little left of the ball's center, so the pole is tilted toward the viewer. The cap is a slightly flattened ellipse. That flattening fits its position: the cap sits about 0.4 of the radius above center, which gives a width-to-height ratio of about 0.92. The seams curve away from the cap like meridians on a sphere and wrap plausibly around the silhouette toward the hidden opposite pole. The gores are about equally wide where they meet the cap. The ball rests on the sand at its lowest point, and its shadow falls to the lower left on the same ground plane, so the ball and the sand share one camera.
